entries.claim: The Latin text in this revision of Divinum Officium is used for comparison with the printed Missal.

locator.section: Rubricae generales Missalis romani, nn. 480–481, 513 a, 514. Ordo Missae. Praefationes in tono solemni.

entries.claim: At the end of the last Secret, the celebrant says aloud or sings Per omnia saecula saeculorum. The response is Amen.

locator.section: Postcommunion, top-right: complete first17 formula words through Deus.

entries.claim: The Postcommunion on printed p.123 prints Per Dominum nostrum ... Deus. in full. Only the middle wording nostrum through Deus (w031–w045) is supplied from this locus; the proper cue supplies Per Dominum. Current Deus, instead of the printed Deus. is declared editorial assembly.

locator.section: First chant line: terminal four words and response Amen; later dialogue excluded

entries.claim: The first chant line on printed p.226 prints Per omnia saecula saeculorum followed by the marked response Amen. This supports the terminal wording w046–w050 after joining chant syllables; current lowercase per is an editorial join. No Mark-specific response actor or first/last commemoration position is inferred.

The cited Benziger proper page prints the 28-word prayer body (w001–w028) and the abbreviated Per Dominum cue (w029–w030). The supplied middle and terminal conclusion wording and Amen are not printed in full on this proper page and have separate same-edition dependencies.

RG115a prescribes the full Father-directed conclusion, including Amen. It supports the common wording supplied after this proper page’s abbreviated cue; its own punctuation/case/accent treatment is not the current continuous reader typography.
